request.spec:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A plan can now name one of its sheet's descendants, and its claims are then made on that sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. After that run I only edited a comment in one YAML file, so I didn't run the tests again.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V91__plan_sheet.sql`, adds a `target_sheet` column to `plan`. It is empty when the plan makes claims on its own sheet.
- **Adding a plan:** the plan form has a new `plan-form-sheet` field. If it isn't blank, the server checks it against the sheet's descendants and refuses anything else with `plan-error`, storing nothing and writing no audit record. When a sheet is named, `PLAN_ADDED` ends with ` sheet=<id>`. Plans with no sheet keep exactly the line they had before.
- **Generating:** `GeneratePlanClaims` looks up the person with the same name on the named sheet. If there isn't one, that plan makes nothing. Otherwise the claims are checked by that sheet's rules and their `CLAIM_ADDED` lines go in that sheet's audit. The count and the plan's own generated count still include them.

Three behaviours to be aware of:
- **Which "today" applies:** plan dates still run up to the plan's own sheet's today, not the named sheet's. The test needs this: the child sheet's today is 03-01, yet claims dated 03-06 and 03-11 are made there.
- **Aliases match:** "same name" uses the existing `findByName` lookup, so a person on the named sheet whose alias matches also counts.
- **Checked once:** the descendant check only happens when the plan is added. If the sheet later stops being a descendant, the plan keeps making claims there.

I also updated the comments on the two plan endpoints to describe the new field.
